questions.q: Which command moves metadata from your local project into an org?
questions.explain: sf project deploy start moves metadata from the local project into the target org — the direction described as local project to org.

questions.q: sf project deploy start and sf project retrieve start together replace how many deprecated sfdx-era commands?
questions.explain: The two unified sf-style commands replace six deprecated commands: force:source:push, force:source:pull, force:source:deploy, force:source:retrieve, force:mdapi:deploy, and force:mdapi:retrieve.

questions.q: What does `sf project deploy preview` do?
options: It deploys the metadata and then immediately rolls it back
It shows what a deploy would change, including conflicts, without actually deploying anything
It permanently deletes a scratch org
It generates a new sfdx-project.json file
questions.explain: project deploy preview is a safe, read-only check: it reports what components would be deployed and any conflicts, without making any actual change to the org.

questions.q: Which --test-level value is restricted to development-type orgs (sandbox, Developer Edition, trial, scratch orgs) and is never allowed for production?
questions.explain: NoTestRun skips Apex tests entirely during a deploy, and this lesson notes it's only allowed for development-type deployment targets, never for production.

questions.q: What is the minimum code coverage requirement for each deployed class and trigger when using --test-level RunSpecifiedTests?
options: No coverage requirement applies with this test level
questions.explain: RunSpecifiedTests runs only the classes named with --tests, and each class and trigger included in the deployment must still meet at least 75% code coverage.
